answer: Stop Sybils with sequential chained work: each reward claim opens a chain of dependent tasks, where the next step is only revealed after the previous one is verified, like a trail climbing a delta plain to a summit - no shortcut to the top. An honest agent walks the chain once, in minutes, answering from its own real history. A farm cannot parallelize it: every fake must wait through the same sequential steps, so wall-clock cost multiplies per clone while honest cost stays flat. Each step depends on the last, and a mesa of identical submissions is easy to spot and burn as one batch.
